items.description: The full name of this platform — an AI-powered system built for Indian law enforcement agencies to automatically trace, attribute, and report on cryptocurrency fraud cases.
The national competition under which this project was built. SIH PS-26183 was issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs, I4C Division.
The central body under the Ministry of Home Affairs responsible for coordinating cybercrime prevention and investigation across India. This platform was built per their problem statement.
The citizen-facing portal (cybercrime.gov.in) where victims report cyber fraud. Suspect wallet addresses reported here feed into ChainSentinel AI investigations.

items.full: System for Automated Help via Yojana and Online Gateway
items.description: A MHA platform used for LEA-VASP coordination to freeze cryptocurrency assets. ChainSentinel AI is designed to integrate with SAHYOG for rapid freeze requests.
The primary users of this platform — police investigators, cybercrime cell officers, and forensic analysts from state/central agencies.
The Government of India ministry that issued this problem statement and oversees I4C and NCRP.

Any exchange, broker, or platform that offers cryptocurrency trading or custody services (e.g., Binance, WazirX, Coinbase). VASP identification is the primary goal of each investigation — if the suspect wallet ultimately reaches a VASP, a legal notice can freeze the funds.
The native token of the Ethereum blockchain. One of the primary chains supported by ChainSentinel AI.
The native token of the TRON blockchain. Frequently used in cyber fraud due to low fees and high throughput. TronGrid API is used for real-time data fetching.
The first and most widely known cryptocurrency. ChainSentinel AI supports UTXO-model tracing for Bitcoin via the Blockchain.info API.
The native token of the Polygon network — an Ethereum Layer-2 chain. Supported via Polygonscan API.
Bitcoin's accounting model. Each transaction consumes previous outputs and creates new ones. Different from the account-based model used by Ethereum and TRON.
Financial services (lending, trading, bridging) built on blockchains without centralised intermediaries. Fraudsters use DeFi protocols to launder funds before reaching a VASP.
A smart-contract-based exchange that swaps tokens without a central authority (e.g., Uniswap, PancakeSwap). DEX hops are detected during Pattern Analysis.
A regulated or semi-regulated exchange with KYC/AML obligations (e.g., Binance, WazirX). The primary target of VASP attribution — these entities can freeze funds.
The process exchanges use to verify user identity. If a suspect wallet reaches a KYC-compliant VASP, LEAs can obtain user details via a legal notice.
Regulatory framework requiring financial institutions (including VASPs) to detect and report suspicious transactions. ChainSentinel AI's risk engine supports AML investigations.
A unique blockchain token representing ownership of a digital asset. NFT wash trading is one of the fraud typologies ChainSentinel AI can flag.
A unique 64-character hexadecimal string that identifies a blockchain transaction. Used as the primary key in the normalised_transactions table.
The fee paid to Ethereum miners/validators to execute a transaction. High gas fees sometimes indicate MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) activity, which can be a fraud signal.
A fraud pattern where a single wallet distributes funds to many sub-wallets simultaneously to obfuscate the trail. Detected when the suspect sends to ≥3 unique destinations.
When funds are forwarded between wallets within a very short time window (<1 hour), indicating deliberate layering to complicate tracing.
When funds pass through a mixing service (e.g., Tornado Cash) that pools and re-distributes coins to break the transaction trail. Highest-risk pattern.
Funds moved from one blockchain to another (e.g., ETH→TRON via THORChain). Complicates investigations requiring analysts to switch chain explorers.
A pattern where small amounts are 'peeled off' at each hop while the bulk continues forward — used to disguise the total fraud amount.
Malware that encrypts victim data and demands cryptocurrency payment for decryption keys. ChainSentinel AI traces ransom wallet addresses to the receiving VASP.
Fraudsters who coerce victims with intimate images and demand crypto payments. Suspect wallet addresses from these cases are among the most common inputs.
Long-con investment fraud where victims are lured onto fake trading platforms and gradually convinced to deposit large sums before being 'slaughtered' (funds stolen).
The graph traversal algorithm used in the Fund Flow Trace stage. Starting from the suspect wallet, BFS explores all neighbours (directly connected wallets) before going deeper.
The data structure used to represent fund flows. Funds travel in one direction (source → destination) without circular paths, making it a DAG.
ML algorithm used in entity matching to score how uniquely an address label identifies a known VASP or entity. Higher TF-IDF score = more confident match.
Pipeline stage 11 — matches graph nodes against the known VASP database (wallets, names, jurisdictions) and produces a confidence score and legal classification (SERVEABLE / UNSERVEABLE).
A score calculated from transaction volume, hop count, fraud patterns found, mixer interactions, and cross-chain activity. 0–39=LOW, 40–59=MEDIUM, 60–79=HIGH, 80+=CRITICAL.
A cryptographic hash function used to generate the integrity fingerprint of each forensic report. Courts can verify a report hasn't been tampered with by re-computing its SHA-256 hash.
Pipeline stage 4 — converts raw API responses from different blockchains into a unified internal schema stored in the normalised_transactions table.

The legal provision under which Indian courts direct VASPs (exchanges) to produce documents and freeze cryptocurrency assets linked to fraud investigations. ChainSentinel AI auto-generates draft notices.
The initial complaint document filed with police in India. The complaint's victim wallet address is the starting point for a ChainSentinel AI investigation.
Indian legislation that criminalises money laundering. Blockchain forensic evidence generated by this platform can support PMLA prosecution.
The global AML/CFT standard-setting body. Its Travel Rule requires VASPs to share sender/receiver information for transactions above a threshold — relevant to cross-border crypto fraud.
Regulatory requirements alongside AML. Crypto transactions linked to terrorist financing triggers a CRITICAL risk score in ChainSentinel AI.
A VASP classification meaning India has a Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT) or direct LEA channel with the VASP's jurisdiction, enabling a legal notice to freeze funds.
A bilateral agreement between countries allowing law enforcement cooperation. VASPs in MLAT-partner jurisdictions are classified as SERVEABLE.
A standardized way for systems to communicate. ChainSentinel AI uses REST APIs from Etherscan, TronGrid, and Chainabuse to fetch live blockchain data.
The architectural style used by ChainSentinel's backend API (NestJS). All frontend-to-backend communication uses REST over HTTP.
The authentication mechanism used by ChainSentinel AI. On login, the server issues a short-lived access token (15 min) and a refresh token (7 days).
Used to push live pipeline stage updates to the frontend during an investigation. As each of the 14 stages completes, the UI updates in real time without polling.
An optional graph database (Bolt protocol) used to persist fund-flow graphs. Falls back to in-memory/PostgreSQL if Neo4j is offline.
The primary database. Hosted on Supabase (ap-northeast-1 region). Stores all investigations, wallets, transactions, reports, VASPs, alerts, and watchlists.
The cloud Postgres hosting provider used in this project. Connection: aws-0-ap-northeast-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432. Credentials are stored in the root .env file.
The ORM library used to define database entities and run queries from NestJS. All tables are auto-created via TypeORM's synchronize mode.
The backend framework powering ChainSentinel's API server (runs on port 3001). Uses decorators and dependency injection.
The frontend framework (runs on port 3000). Uses the App Router, server components, and client components for the dashboard UI.
The package manager used in this monorepo workspace. Faster and more disk-efficient than npm or yarn.
The library used to render the interactive Transaction Graph with nodes, edges, zoom, pan, and minimap.
Manages the monorepo containing apps/api and apps/web. The run.bat script uses Turborepo to start both simultaneously.
The official TRON Foundation API for fetching transaction history from TRON addresses. Endpoint: api.trongrid.io. API key stored in the blockchain_api_configs table.
Multi-chain Ethereum ecosystem data API. Supports ETH, Polygon, BSC, and others via chainid parameter. Endpoint: api.etherscan.io/v2/api.
Community-sourced database of flagged wallet addresses linked to scams, ransomware, and phishing. Used as a supplementary OSINT source.
Used optionally for job queuing and caching. Falls back gracefully if not running.
Publicly available information used in investigations. Chainabuse reports, public blockchain labels (Etherscan tags), and wallet clustering datasets are OSINT sources.
The home dashboard — shows live stats (active investigations, flagged wallets, risk distribution, recent activity) pulled from the Postgres database.
Displays all known VASPs in the database with their jurisdiction, known wallet addresses, confidence score, and chain coverage.
Search for any wallet address across all investigations. Shows transaction history, risk score, attribution history, and watchlist status.
Interactive BFS-layout graph that shows how funds flow from a suspect wallet through intermediaries to exchanges. Nodes are colour-coded by type.
Search any transaction hash or address directly against live blockchain APIs without creating a formal investigation.
Groups of related fraud wallets clustered into a single campaign. Helps identify organised cybercrime rings operating across multiple victims.
Tracks fund movements across blockchain bridges (THORChain, Multichain, etc.) to follow money that moves between Ethereum, TRON, Bitcoin, and other chains.
Generates a pre-filled draft legal notice addressed to the identified VASP, requesting account freeze and KYC records, per Section 91 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Real-time status of all backend services: PostgreSQL, Neo4j, Redis, WebSocket gateway, ETH provider, and TRON provider. Auto-refreshes every 15 seconds.
Admin panel to manage blockchain data provider configurations (endpoint URLs, API keys, chain IDs, rate limits). Located under Administration → System Settings.
